candidate: South Bison Hill prototype reclamation covers
location: Syncrude Mildred Lake Mine, Alberta, Canada
fatal_blocker: The public primary papers and Syncrude synthesis describe prescribed or nominal cover configurations of 35, 50 and 100 cm, but do not publish final measured as-built thickness values, numerical thickness uncertainty, survey accuracy, surveyed plot-corner coordinates, or a georeferenced polygon deliverable. The approximately 50 m-wide plots contain extensive monitoring and drainage infrastructure, so a 30-40 m clean interior cannot be established from public geometry after exclusions. The D3 surface layer also contained unintended secondary-material inclusions and initially supported sparser vegetation, weakening the matched-surface assumption.
key_evidence: Three adjacent one-hectare covers were constructed on a north-facing approximately 5:1 slope in 1999.
The 50 cm and 100 cm prescriptions both use a 20 cm peat/glacial surface layer over different thicknesses of secondary subsoil.
The public literature calls these reclamation prescriptions or cover depths and does not publish a final as-built thickness survey.
No public numerical depth tolerance, horizontal or vertical survey accuracy, or exact plot-corner coordinate table was found.
Each plot includes midslope instrumentation, neutron access tubes at top/middle/toe positions, interflow cutoff and collection systems, runoff swales and weirs.
The D3 peat surface layer contained unintended secondary-material inclusions and vegetation was initially less established than on the thinner covers.
Later research confirms long-term monitoring and forest development, but does not tie a repair-free Sentinel-1 window to exact public calibration polygons.
